To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presented architecture is capable of providing a unified management plane for SDNs and legacy networks.

we propose a unified management interface that enables vendor-neutral programmability for the management plane of SDN and legacy network devices and that we show its applicability by example of a proof-of-concepts implementation.

the proposed architecture enables a programmable management of heterogeneous networks, while providing a vendor-neutral and device-neutral abstraction of the management plane, and preventing undesired side-effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following research questions: How can we enable programmability of the management plane in heterogeneous networks?
the development and evaluation of a unified interface to SDN and legacy network devices, with the aim of facilitating the development of management applications.
the programmability of the management plane and the development of a vendor-neutral management plane abstraction layer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the architecture is a promising step towards programmability of the management plane.
our work is a first step towards a programmable management layer for SDN and traditional networks, and that we provide a solid base for the future development of a unified management layer.
we provide a proof of concept that a vendor-neutral management plane for SDNs and legacy devices is possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel approach for a programmable management interface for heterogeneous networks.
our approach provides the first step to enable a vendor-neutral and programmable management plane.

the proposed abstraction layer provides a vendor-neutral and device-neutral management interface, which is well prepared against undesireable side-effects, while being able to operate with legacy devices and SDN controllers in parallel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a unified management plane is feasible and that it can provide a solid foundation for a programmable and vendor-neutral management plane.
the proposed architecture enables a vendor-neutral management plane for heterogeneous network devices, while preserving the benefits of SDN programmability.
the proposed architecture enables the development of vendor-neutral and domain-agnostic management applications for heterogeneous networks.
